findings.title: Missing Security Header: Content-Security-Policy (CSP)
findings.description: Content-Security-Policy helps prevent Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), data injection, and clickjacking attacks.
findings.evidence: HTTP response headers returned from http://127.0.0.1:8888 did not include 'content-security-policy'.
findings.remediation: Implement a strong Content-Security-Policy header restricting script-src, object-src, and default-src directives.

findings.title: Missing Security Header: X-Frame-Options (Clickjacking Protection)
findings.description: Missing X-Frame-Options header allows malicious websites to embed this site in an <iframe> for clickjacking attacks.
findings.evidence: HTTP response headers returned from http://127.0.0.1:8888 did not include 'x-frame-options'.
findings.remediation: Set 'X-Frame-Options: DENY' or 'X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN' to prevent framing attacks.

findings.title: Missing Security Header: X-Content-Type-Options (MIME-Sniffing)
findings.description: Without this header, older browsers might inspect response contents and execute malicious scripts disguised as images or text.
findings.evidence: HTTP response headers returned from http://127.0.0.1:8888 did not include 'x-content-type-options'.
findings.remediation: Set 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff' to disable MIME-type sniffing.

findings.title: Missing Security Header: Referrer-Policy
findings.description: Specifies how much referrer information (URL parameters, tokens) is sent along with requests.
findings.evidence: HTTP response headers returned from http://127.0.0.1:8888 did not include 'referrer-policy'.
findings.remediation: Set 'Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin' or 'no-referrer'.

findings.title: Missing Security Header: Permissions-Policy
findings.description: Permissions-Policy allows site administrators to declare which browser features can be used.
findings.evidence: HTTP response headers returned from http://127.0.0.1:8888 did not include 'permissions-policy'.
findings.remediation: Implement Permissions-Policy to explicitly declare allowed browser features (camera, microphone, geolocation).

findings.title: Web Server Banner Disclosure
findings.description: The server exposes internal technology and version details via the 'server' header.
findings.evidence: Header 'server: uvicorn, Apache/2.4.41 (Ubuntu) PHP/7.4.3' was found in the HTTP response.
findings.remediation: Configure the web server or reverse proxy to strip or obscure the 'server' header.

findings.title: Backend Technology / Framework Disclosure
findings.description: The server exposes internal technology and version details via the 'x-powered-by' header.
findings.evidence: Header 'x-powered-by: PHP/7.4.3' was found in the HTTP response.
findings.remediation: Configure the web server or reverse proxy to strip or obscure the 'x-powered-by' header.

findings.title: Insecure Cookie: Missing HttpOnly Flag (session_id)
findings.description: Cookie 'session_id' lacks the HttpOnly attribute, making it accessible to client-side JavaScript and vulnerable to theft via XSS.
findings.evidence: Set-Cookie: session_id=dummy_session_12345; Path=/; SameSite=lax
findings.remediation: Add the 'HttpOnly' flag to all sensitive and session cookies.

findings.title: Exposed Spring Boot Actuator Environment (/actuator/env)
findings.description: Spring Boot Actuator '/env' endpoint is exposed without authentication, leaking internal environment properties and credentials.
findings.remediation: Disable or enforce strict Spring Security authentication on all '/actuator/*' endpoints.

findings.title: Open Redirect in Parameter 'url'
findings.description: The endpoint accepts an untrusted destination URL in parameter 'url' and redirects users without validation, facilitating phishing and credential theft.
findings.evidence:
Open Redirect detected on parameter 'url':
Request URL: http://127.0.0.1:8888/redirect?url=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Fsec-probe-redirect
Technique: Direct HTTPS URL
Status Code: 302
Location Header: https://example.com/sec-probe-redirect
findings.remediation: Implement a whitelist of approved redirect URLs, or restrict redirects strictly to relative paths starting with a single forward slash.

findings.title: API1: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA / IDOR)
findings.description: The API allows accessing object records across different IDs without validating user authorization or tenant ownership.
findings.evidence:
Potential BOLA / IDOR vulnerability on endpoint:
Original: http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/users/1 -> HTTP 200
Mutated Object ID: http://127.0.0.1:8888/api/users/2 -> HTTP 200
Response preview:
{"id":2,"username":"bob","email":"bob@company.internal","credit_card":"5424-9876-5432-1098","role":"user"}
findings.remediation: Implement authorization checks verifying that the currently logged-in user has permission to read or manipulate the requested object ID.

findings.title: API4: Unrestricted Resource Consumption (Missing Rate Limiting)
findings.description: The API endpoint lacks rate limiting or request throttling, leaving it vulnerable to Denial of Service (DoS) and brute force attacks.
findings.evidence:
Sent 12 rapid consecutive requests to 'http://127.0.0.1:8888/'.
All 12 requests returned HTTP 200 OK without rate-limiting headers or HTTP 429 status.
findings.remediation: Implement rate limiting (e.g., token bucket, redis-based rate limiting) and return HTTP 429 Too Many Requests with standard Retry-After headers.
